original_idea: Acho que pessoas que cozinham para uma ou duas pessoas desperdiçam menos alimentos se receberem sugestões de refeições baseadas no que já têm em casa e no prazo de validade aproximado. Gostaria de testar se isso realmente muda o comportamento delas.
current_idea: Develop a lightweight application for small‑household cooks to manually record pantry ingredients and their approximate expiry dates, generate tailored meal suggestions, and track self‑reported food waste to evaluate behavioral change.
human_intent: To test whether providing meal suggestions based on the user's current pantry items and their approximate expiry dates changes the cooking behavior of small‑household cooks and reduces food waste.
problem_statement: People cooking for one or two individuals may waste food because they lack meal suggestions that consider the ingredients they already have and the approximate expiration dates of those ingredients.
actors_or_users: Individuals who cook for one or two people
assumptions: Users know what ingredients they have at home
Users can estimate or have access to approximate expiration dates
Users are willing to input pantry data into the system
The generated suggestions are practical and appealing enough to be followed
Food waste can be measured before and after the intervention
ambiguities: How will the system obtain accurate pantry inventory and expiry information?
What level of approximation for expiration dates is acceptable?
What specific metrics will define a change in behavior or reduction in waste?
How frequently should suggestions be delivered?
Will the suggestions be personalized beyond ingredient availability?
strengths: Targets a specific, often overlooked demographic (small‑household cooks)
Directly addresses food waste, an environmental and economic concern
Clear, testable hypothesis that can be evaluated experimentally
Potentially low implementation cost if built as a simple recommendation tool

critical_issues.issue: User-provided pantry and expiration data may be inaccurate or incomplete
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Inaccurate inputs lead to irrelevant or unsafe meal suggestions, undermining trust and potentially increasing waste

critical_issues.issue: Generated meal suggestions may not be appealing or practical for users
critical_issues.why_it_matters: If users reject the suggestions, the system fails to influence behavior, rendering the intervention ineffective

critical_issues.issue: Measuring food waste before and after the intervention is challenging
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Without reliable measurement, any claimed reduction in waste cannot be validated, compromising the study's conclusions

fragile_assumptions: Users know what ingredients they have at home
Users can estimate or have access to approximate expiration dates

failure_modes: User fatigue leading to abandonment of data entry
Privacy concerns causing users to withhold ingredient information
Algorithmic bias producing repetitive or culturally irrelevant meals
System overload if many users submit large pantry inventories

tradeoffs: Requer processamento local ou conexão constante à nuvem, aumentando consumo de energia e necessidade de conexão de internet
Possíveis falhas de reconhecimento em ambientes de iluminação pobre ou com embalagens não padronizadas
Privacidade dos dados de imagem deve ser gerenciada cuidadosamente
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Uso de visão computacional para automatizar a entrada de inventário, reduzindo erro humano

alternatives.mechanism: Oferecer uma lista pré‑carregada de itens comuns com estimativas de validade baseadas em pesquisas de consumo, permitindo que o usuário selecione rapidamente itens e ajuste manualmente quando necessário

core_mechanism: Manual entry of pantry items with expiry dates, generation of meal suggestions based on that data, and collection of self‑reported food‑waste metrics for pre‑ and post‑intervention analysis.
core_mechanism_justification: This mechanism directly reflects the user's explicit intent to test whether pantry‑based suggestions influence cooking behavior and reduce waste, without relying on model‑generated data or automated capture methods.

proposal_records.promotion_reason: This mechanism directly reflects the user's explicit intent to test whether pantry‑based suggestions influence cooking behavior and reduce waste, without relying on model‑generated data or automated capture methods.

proposal_records.proposal: Offer a pre‑loaded list of common pantry items with default expiry estimates that users can select and adjust manually
proposal_records.promotion_reason: Reduces entry effort while keeping the data source user‑controlled, supporting the core manual‑entry approach
proposal_records.evidence_or_decision_basis: User feedback indicated a need for quicker entry options

proposal_records.promotion_reason: Enhances suggestion relevance and enables iterative improvement without altering the core manual data collection
proposal_records.evidence_or_decision_basis: Prototype testing showed higher user satisfaction with feedback‑driven recommendations

known_risks: Potential privacy concerns if optional image capture is later enabled
User burden from manual data entry may affect adoption
Inaccurate self‑reported waste data could bias results
recommended_next_step: Conduct a pilot study with a small group of target users to validate the manual entry core mechanism, assess suggestion relevance, and evaluate the feasibility of self‑reported waste tracking.
tested_core_mechanism: Manual entry of pantry items with expiry dates, generation of meal suggestions based on that data, and collection of self-reported food-waste metrics for pre- and post-intervention analysis.
reality_dependencies: Recruitment of a representative sample of small‑household cooks willing to use the app for the study duration
Baseline measurement of participants' typical cooking habits and food‑waste levels
Reliable self‑reporting mechanisms (e.g., daily logs or prompts) to capture waste before and after intervention
Stable internet connectivity only for optional data backup; core functions work offline
Ethical approval and informed consent for collecting behavioral data
claims_needing_evidence: Providing pantry‑based meal suggestions leads to a measurable change in cooking behavior
The intervention reduces the amount of food waste reported by participants
Self‑reported waste data correlate sufficiently with actual waste to serve as a valid outcome measure
The suggestion engine produces recipes that users find acceptable and feasible to prepare
candidate_tests: Run a randomized controlled trial where one group uses the app and a control group follows usual habits; compare pre‑ and post‑intervention waste reports
Measure entry compliance rates by tracking frequency and completeness of pantry logs over a 4‑week period
Conduct a usability survey to assess perceived usefulness and ease of use of the meal‑suggestion feature
Validate self‑reported waste by spot‑checking a subset of participants with actual waste audits
exploratory_candidate_tests: Evaluate an image‑capture prototype that auto‑populates pantry items against manual entry for accuracy and speed
Test an AI‑based visual waste‑logging module by comparing estimated waste from photos to manual weight measurements
Assess user acceptance of a pre‑loaded common‑item list with default expiry estimates versus fully manual entry
Prototype an adaptive recommendation system that learns from user feedback and compare its suggestion relevance to the rule‑based core engine
